title: UnoArena — Async spine
description: The log-before-broadcast spine: two outbox relays, six consumer groups, the reconciler and the timer worker. Every relay panel is grouped by job — the two relays publish to different topics and a summed panel would hide one of them going idle.

options.content:
**Every relay panel is `by (job)`.** `outbox-relay` drains room-gameplay's outbox, `outbox-relay-tournament` drains the tournament's — one image, two Deployments, two scrape jobs. Summed, one relay stopping is invisible.

**Every gauge here is paired with a success counter.** `backlog_rows` and `lag_seconds` both read `0` from a relay that has never once reached its database — the healthiest possible reading. `backlog_reads_total` is what tells the two apart.

**`consumer_starts_total` at 0 while the pod is Running means the consumer never started.** A projection counter at 0 cannot otherwise be told from "nobody has played a game yet": that cost 13 minutes of silent outage in P6.

**`tournament_commands_contended_total` moving a little is a registration rush.** A lot means the retry budget is too small for the contention.

panels.title: Outbox relays — rows published per second, by relay and topic
panels.description: Both relays run the same binary with four env knobs changed. If one line flattens while the other keeps moving, the producer behind it has stopped or its relay has.

panels.title: Outbox backlog and lag, with the read counter that makes a zero meaningful
panels.description: lag_seconds is the age of the oldest unpublished row and is the first number to go wrong when Kafka is unreachable. If backlog_reads is flat at the same time, the relay is not reading the database at all and the two zeroes above it mean nothing.

panels.title: Consumer lag, by group and topic
panels.description: Six groups read this spine: ranking-elo, ranking-placement, tournament-saga, analytics-projections, spectator-view and room-gameplay. Lag that climbs and does not come back is a consumer that has stopped keeping up; lag that is flat at zero next to a lag_reads counter that is also flat is a consumer that is not measuring at all.

panels.title: Consumer starts — has each consumer ever entered its poll loop?
panels.description: Zero here while the pod is Running is the P6 failure exactly: kafkajs exhausted its own retries during a cold start, start() rejected, a .catch that only logged left the service alive with no consumer, and /health answered 200 for thirteen minutes. Any value above one means the consumer has restarted its loop, which is the healthy backoff doing its job.

panels.title: Events consumed, projected and deduped
panels.description: Deduped moving is not a fault — at-least-once delivery means a redelivery is expected, and consumed_events refusing it is the guarantee working. Deduped climbing while projected stays flat is a consumer stuck redelivering one batch.

panels.title: Skipped and rejected events, by reason
panels.description: A consumer skipping an event type it has no use for is correct and counted on purpose. This panel is what turned a whole class of silent bug visible in P6: ranking read four lifecycle events and scored none of them, because it compared ce-type (a reverse-DNS URI) to a bare event name — invisible without a skip counter carrying the reason.

panels.title: Contended tournament commands — the metric P7 said to watch
panels.description: A command that exhausted its optimistic-concurrency attempts. It returns 409 and the client retries — it must never return success, which is the defect P7's review pass found in the one path where the reconciler races the saga by design. A few during a registration rush is the design working; a sustained climb means the retry budget is too small for the contention.

panels.title: The two sweepers — reconciler and timer worker
panels.description: Both are designed to race the thing they repair, and both are idempotent. due_rooms is a gauge and reads 0 both when there is nothing due and when the worker has never swept — which is why sweeps_total is plotted next to it. The timer worker is also the recovery path that unstuck four tournaments at once in P7 when its token was fixed.

panels.title: Consumer errors and the timer worker's tick lag
panels.description: Tick lag is how late a deadline was resolved relative to when it fell due — the number that went wrong invisibly in P7 when the timer worker's pod held a Secret without the internal token and 401'd on every tick.
